Born: October 21, 1980, 10:46 AM local time, Los Angeles, California, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the time comes from a birth certificate or an equally solid record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read at face value. Open Kim Kardashian's chart on Astrolas to follow the wheel while you read.

One feature sits at the top of the chart and holds the whole thing together. Jupiter sits at the very tip of Virgo, almost exactly on the Midheaven, the point that marks career and public standing. Saturn and Pluto sit nearby in Libra, in the same 10th house. Three planets, one house: the house of how the world sees you and what you build there.

muc.ten: Jupiter on the Midheaven, with Saturn and Pluto close behind
doan: Jupiter sits at 28°52' Virgo, the Midheaven at 28°27' Virgo, a conjunction with an orb of just 0°26'. That's as tight as a major angle gets. The Astrolas library reads Jupiter conjunct the Midheaven as a mix of career success and a prosperous household, built on a combination of luck and sustained effort, with a caution against coasting and a reminder to keep ambition from crowding out private life.

The library's Jupiter in Virgo adds the method behind it: intelligence, sharp analysis, and a habit of turning a talent into paying work, built step by step rather than overnight. Jupiter in the 10th house, in the library's terms, points to fortune in advancement and a name that carries weight in its field, so long as confidence doesn't tip into overreach.

Saturn sits at 3°41' Libra, also in the 10th house, conjunct Jupiter at an orb of 4°49'. The library reads Jupiter conjunct Saturn as idealism meeting obstacles, with persistence as the only way through and a payoff that is slow but lasting. Saturn in Libra, per the library, favors clear judgment and diplomacy and suits law, the arts or any public-facing role; Saturn in the 10th adds that success tends to arrive late, often after 30, built on self-reliance rather than a head start. Kim Kardashian began studying law through California's apprenticeship route in her late 30s, a multi-year path toward the bar that she has worked at alongside running her businesses, which fits a Saturn that pays out late and only through sustained effort.

Pluto sits at 21°58' Libra, also in the 10th house. Pluto in Libra is generational, a signature the library ties to the years 1971 to 1984 rather than to her alone; the personal layer comes through the house. The library's Pluto in the 10th reads as ambition for power and a career that moves through real transformation, built on instinct for who to trust in a competitive field. She has built and sold stakes in more than one company, from a cosmetics line to a shapewear brand that grew into a business valued in the billions, each one a different shape of the same drive.

muc.ten: Sun and Mercury in the 11th house, Libra and Scorpio
doan: The Sun sits at 28°29' Libra and Mercury at 19°48' Scorpio, both in the 11th house. The library's Libra Sun describes charm, fairness and a gift for making others comfortable, suited to work in fashion, design or anything that calls for diplomacy. In the 11th house, the library ties the Sun to deep, lasting friendships across very different circles, a talent for pulling people into an ever-widening group, and a focus on purpose over personal credit.

Mercury in Scorpio, per the library, is a mind that wants the truth under the surface, speaks only when there is something worth saying, and sticks with a position once it is made up. Mercury in the 11th reads as an extroverted, adaptable communicator whose friendships tend to run on shared ideas rather than small talk. Kim Kardashian's public life started as part of a group, a reality show built around her entire family, and her career since has run largely through audiences and platforms rather than solo output.

Mercury also sits close to Uranus, a conjunction with an orb of 4°24'. The library reads this pairing as a breakthrough aspect: progressive, original thinking and a communication style striking enough to leave an impression, paired with a restless mind that needs an anchor to stay focused. The tightest aspect in the whole chart sits elsewhere: Mercury sextile Venus, orb just 0°12', though the library has no text yet for that pairing.

muc.ten: Moon in Pisces in the 3rd house, opposite the career cluster
doan: The Moon sits at 28°09' Pisces in the 3rd house. The library's Pisces Moon runs on sensitivity and intuition, feels the world through a romantic, sometimes blurred lens, and carries real creative, even psychic, ability, alongside a tendency to drift from reality under pressure. In the 3rd house, the library ties that emotional tone to communication and memory: thought and feeling blend together, the memory holds detail well, and bonds with siblings and neighbors run on quiet, frequent contact rather than declarations.

That last point lines up with the public record. Kim Kardashian's fame began on a reality show built around her whole family, her sisters and brother included, and a Moon in the 3rd house of siblings and daily talk fits a career that started as a family conversation broadcast outward.

The Moon also opposes the Midheaven, orb just 0°17', and opposes Jupiter at 0°43'. Both sit on the same axis as the career cluster above, though the library has no text yet for either pairing, so they stand here only as structure: the private, feeling side of the chart sits in direct tension with the public, built side.

muc.ten: Venus in Virgo in the 9th house, square Neptune
doan: Venus sits at 19°36' Virgo in the 9th house. The library's Virgo Venus is selective and slow to open up, with high standards that soften once trust is earned, paired with real business sense and a frugal streak. In the 9th house, the library reads a love of education, culture and travel, drawn to partners or settings a little larger than life, with a caution to keep that idealism grounded in what actually works.

Venus squares Neptune at an orb of 0°59', just under a full degree. The library has no text for this pairing, but the shape fits: Virgo's practical standards pulling against Neptune's gloss, business sense set beside image. Her ventures sit at exactly that intersection of practical product and image, from a cosmetics line to a shapewear brand built around the body itself.

muc.ten: Mars in Sagittarius in the 12th house
doan: Mars sits at 6°48' Sagittarius in the 12th house. The library's Sagittarius Mars is bold, adventurous and quick to start something new, driven by belief and principle more than caution, with a competitive streak that tends to land on its feet. In the 12th house, the library describes that drive turned inward: ambition held close rather than announced, real compassion for people lower down the ladder expressed quietly, and a need to release that energy in healthy ways rather than let it build.
Mars sextiles Saturn at an orb of 3°07', another pairing the library hasn't written up yet, linking that inward drive to the same Saturn anchoring the career cluster above.

muc.ten: Ascendant in Sagittarius, with Neptune in the 1st house
doan: The birth record puts the Ascendant at 13°44' Sagittarius, the Descendant at 13°44' Gemini, and, as covered above, the Midheaven at 28°27' Virgo with the IC at 28°27' Pisces. The Astrolas library doesn't yet have entries for Sagittarius rising or a Gemini Descendant, so this piece won't build a reading on the Ascendant sign itself.

Neptune sits in the same sign and house, at 20°35' Sagittarius in the 1st house. The library calls Neptune in Sagittarius a generational placement, tied for that generation to a pull toward meaning, belief and other cultures. Its 1st-house reading is personal: an artistic, sensitive presence that adapts to a room like a chameleon, charm that draws people in without an obvious reason, balanced by a need to stay grounded so confidence doesn't slide into doubt. Built across nearly two decades of television, product launches and a public image remade more than once, that fits a persona shaped on purpose.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: Nothing here explains fame by itself, and a chart never does that. What it shows is where the weight sits: a career cluster at the very top of the chart, pulling in Jupiter, Saturn and Pluto, with the Sun and Mercury next door in a house built on networks and groups, and a Pisces Moon underneath, tied to siblings and daily routine, pulling in the opposite direction the whole time.
